title: How one expired key became an 18x origin spike
summary: Walk from the normal cache path through the stampede, delayed detection, and request-coalescing recovery.

truthLadder.analogy: A cache miss is like a shop running out of a popular item; without coordination, every customer asks the warehouse at once.
truthLadder.technical: The observed key expiry removed the fast path, concurrent misses reached origin, origin QPS rose 18x, latency alerts fired four minutes later, and request coalescing restored service.
truthLadder.caveat: The fixture does not prove what made the key simultaneously popular; that trigger remains inferred.

scenes.title: Before the incident
scenes.summary: Requests usually terminate at the hot cache entry instead of reaching origin.

nodes.label: Hot cache entry
nodes.detail: Returns the object without origin work.

scenes.title: Expiry opens the floodgate
scenes.summary: Many concurrent misses fan out to origin before a fresh value is available.

nodes.label: Popular key expires
nodes.detail: The cached value is no longer usable.

failure.impact: The cache no longer absorbs requests for this key
failure.symptom: Concurrent requests all observe a miss
failure.fallback: Coordinate one refresh and let peers wait or serve stale data

nodes.label: Misses fan out
nodes.detail: Requests independently ask origin for the same object.

nodes.label: Origin reaches 18x QPS
nodes.detail: The downstream service receives the amplified load.

failure.impact: Origin capacity is consumed by duplicate work
failure.symptom: Latency rises while QPS is 18 times the prior level
failure.fallback: Coalesce duplicate requests and restore the cache path

scenes.title: Detection arrives, then coordination restores service
scenes.summary: The alert lags the load spike; request coalescing removes duplicate origin work.

nodes.label: Latency alert at +4 min
nodes.detail: Monitoring surfaces user-visible degradation four minutes after the QPS rise.

nodes.label: Request coalescing
nodes.detail: One refresh proceeds while equivalent requests share its result.

nodes.label: Service restored
nodes.detail: Duplicate origin work falls and the cache path recovers.

glossary.definition: Many requests miss the same cache entry and create duplicate downstream work.
Combining equivalent in-flight requests so that one refresh supplies multiple waiters.

teachBack.question: Why did a single key expiry affect origin QPS?
teachBack.answer: Concurrent requests missed the same entry and independently created duplicate origin work.

teachBack.question: Which part of this incident is still uncertain?
teachBack.answer: The trigger that made the key simultaneously hot is inferred; the fixture does not prove it.

evidence.label: Synthetic postmortem input fixture
evidence.note: Directly supports the expiry, 18x QPS, four-minute alert lag, and coalescing recovery claims within this test.

evidence.label: Simultaneous popularity trigger
evidence.note: The input says this trigger remains unproven, so the explainer labels it inferred.

evidence.label: Shop and warehouse analogy
evidence.note: Only illustrates duplicate demand; it does not describe the cache implementation.
